verdict.rationale: Vercel documents its own access tokens that can be scoped to a full account, a team, or a single project. A project-scoped token denies requests to other projects and to user- or team-level resources, which keeps tools and workflows constrained, so agents can be given resource-limited credentials. Least privilege is shown only at the resource-boundary level: there is no documented permission-level scoping (e.g., read-only versus deploy) or agent-specific credential issuance, and there is no hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: fine-grained permission/action scopes (read-only, deploy-only), agent-specific credential issuance or expiry/rotation controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: A project-scoped token denies any request to another project, to a user-level resource, or to a team-level resource. This keeps jobs, tools, and workflows constrained to the projects they need rather than granting them the entire team or your full account.
Create and scope Vercel access tokens to your full account, a team, or a single project, then use them to authenticate API and CLI requests.
Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf.
